speaker: AJ Loiacono

en: Yeah, you don't want to have like new in your name.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah, it's not a high-risk area.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah.

speaker: AJ Loiacono

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But we started as Capital RX, and the concept was let's process these benefits, but unlike our competitors, let's not make money on drugs bed.

speaker: AJ Loiacono

en: But also in that moment, the entire industry realizes if I become what's called vertically integrated, I'm not just the administrator, I own the pharmacy.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I own the rebate aggregation.
zh: 我拥有返点聚合业务。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'll own these other assets so I could get paid multiple times on the same transaction.
zh: 我会拥有这些其他资产，这样我就能在同一笔交易上多次收钱。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So not only am I making money as the administrator, I'm making money possibly on the fulfillment side of the pharmacy, but I'm also making money on what we call like GPO and rebate.
zh: 所以我不仅作为管理方赚钱，我可能还在药房的履约端赚钱，而且我还在我们所谓的 GPO 和返点上赚钱。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so if you could stack this, you make more money.
zh: 所以如果你能把这些叠加起来，你就能赚更多的钱。

zh: 这个利益冲突是，想想看，如果你请某人来管理你的福利计划，而药物越贵，他们赚的钱就越多。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That doesn't sound like a recipe for good outcomes for either the patient population or the plan's cost.
zh: 这听起来不像是能给患者群体或计划成本带来好结果的配方。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so we started as this scrappy company, Capital RX, and the concept was very simple.

en: And this is what I observed over my career.
zh: 这就是我在职业生涯中观察到的情况。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I came from pharmaceutical manufacturing.
zh: 我来自制药生产领域。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So think of it as kind of if you come from the sell side on some level, like, hey, I'm a pharmaceutical manufacturer and I manufacture this product.
zh: 所以可以把它理解为，某种程度上你来自卖方，比如，嘿，我是一家制药厂商，我生产这个产品。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then I move over to the buy side, which is the insurance, if you will, or the administrative side.
zh: 然后我转到买方，也就是保险，可以这么说，或者是管理端。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You would think that these prices would be very tightly correlated.
zh: 你会认为这些价格会高度相关。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: There wouldn't be a lot of variance.
zh: 不会有太大的差异。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But what I discovered made no sense.
zh: 但我发现的情况完全说不通。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So on the manufacturing side, we change price twice a year.
zh: 在生产端，我们一年改两次价格。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You could set a clock to it, January and July.
zh: 你可以拿钟表来对时，一月和七月。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I talk about this all the time.
zh: 我一直在讲这个。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And why you you change prices like each year, they just go up, sort of thing, or you change them for a specific.
zh: 以及为什么你每年都改价格，它们就是往上涨，诸如此类，或者你为了某个特定的原因改价格。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So the way that manufacturing works is you normally in the United States, you escalate the price.
zh: 生产端的运作方式是，通常在美国，你会逐步提价。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And the reason why the defense of the pharmaceutical industry is you have a short patent life before your patent expires.
zh: 而制药行业为之辩护的理由是，在你的专利到期之前，你有一个很短的专利生命周期。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you've put maybe billions of dollars of RD.
zh: 而且你可能已经投入了几十亿美元的 RD。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So you have a finite window before your product goes generic.
zh: 所以在你的产品变成仿制药之前，你有一个有限的时间窗口。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So typically it's stepping up.
zh: 所以通常是逐步上调。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Some of the inflation is natural.
zh: 有些涨价是自然的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It's just general inflation of cost of goods, marketing, market access.
zh: 只是一般性的成本上涨，商品成本、营销、市场准入。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But some of it is driven by the very system I'm describing because the people that are on what I call the buy side, the insurance, are increasing price because they're creating what I would say games around how people access medication.
zh: 但其中一部分是由我正在描述的这个体系本身驱动的，因为处于我所说的买方，也就是保险那边的人，在提高价格，因为他们在围绕人们如何获取药物制造我所说的游戏。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And these are called things like formularies.
zh: 这些被称为诸如处方集之类的东西。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: These are games around market access, and we could talk about that more.
zh: 这些是围绕市场准入的游戏，我们可以再多聊聊这个。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But but the really the essence of it was I came from a world in which pricing was very static.
zh: 但真正的核心是，我来自一个定价非常静态的世界。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You would know in January there's a price increase of 5%, and there'll be another 5% increase in July.
zh: 你会知道一月有 5% 的提价，七月还会有另外 5% 的提价。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But now I'm looking at prices on the insurance side, and you've got 600 prices in one quarter.
zh: 但现在我看保险端的价格，一个季度里有 600 种价格。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I don't want to get too into the weeds, but just a simple example of why would they charge so many different prices to different customers?
zh: 我不想扯得太细，但举一个简单的例子：他们为什么要对不同客户收这么多不同的价格？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like what's what's driving that?
zh: 就像，是什么在驱动这个？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Well, this is what I realized is who loves opacity and variability, people that are seeking the highest level of profitability.
zh: 嗯，这就是我意识到的：谁喜欢不透明和可变性？是那些追求最高盈利水平的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so if they were just plain administrators like we are, just charge a flat fee, you would be forcing these prices to become stable and very transparent to all of your customers.
zh: 所以如果他们只是像我们这样的纯粹管理者，只收固定费用，你就会被迫让这些价格变得稳定，并且对所有客户都非常透明。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But they were doing the opposite.
zh: 但他们做的恰恰相反。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They were putting gag orders, they were making it impossible to get your claims data.
zh: 他们在下达封口令，他们让你根本拿不到自己的理赔数据。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're creating confusion in the market, they're creating unnecessary opacity and complexity.
zh: 他们在市场上制造混乱，制造不必要的不透明和复杂性。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's like crazy segmentation, like hyper-segmentation.
zh: 就像疯狂的细分，超级细分。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Every customer is a different book, depending on your need, your budget, your whatever, I charge you what I can, sort of thing.
zh: 每个客户都是不同的一本账，取决于你的需求、你的预算、你的随便什么，我能收你多少就收多少，诸如此类。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Well, that's exactly it.
zh: 嗯，正是如此。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And, you know, I would say there's some science behind this.
zh: 而且，你知道，我想说这背后是有一些科学依据的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So most people, if you are accepting your prescription at the register, you're going to see pickup of like 96%.
zh: 所以大多数人，如果你是在收银台取你的处方药，取药率大概是 96%。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So think about it.
zh: 你想想看。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: If you're testing how people respond to higher and lower price, if the house knows, in this case the insurance side, that 96% of the time you're just going to take whatever I give you, that's a pretty good number, you know, to work with.
zh: 如果你在测试人们对更高和更低价格的反应，如果庄家——在这个例子中是保险方——知道 96% 的情况下你只会接受我给你的一切，那这是一个相当好用的数字，你知道吗。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so again, the variability was artificial.
zh: 所以再说一次，这种可变性是人为制造的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: This was my big observation.
zh: 这是我最大的观察。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And, you know, the other thing you come to in the gritty days, I can't be the only person that's making this observation.
zh: 而且，你知道，在那段艰难的日子里你还会想到：我不可能是唯一有这个观察的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And the reality is other people are, but they're on the payroll of the model.
zh: 而现实是确实有其他人有，但他们在那个模式的工资单上。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So if someone's like, hey, I'm a consultant or a broker and they get paid on product.
zh: 所以如果有人说，嘿，我是顾问或者经纪人，他们是按产品拿钱的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You want to know who loves bad product?
zh: 你想知道谁喜欢糟糕的产品吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The person who's getting commission on the product.
zh: 是那个从产品上拿佣金的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so now you're not just up against three giants, you know, CVS Cigna United, but you're also up against all the people on the payroll of CVS Cigno United.
zh: 所以现在你不只是对抗三个巨头，你知道，CVS、Cigna、United，你还在对抗所有在 CVS、Cigno、United 工资单上的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that is deep and wide.
zh: 而那既深又广。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so you become enemy number one because you're basically calling out the insurance industry for what it is.
zh: 所以你成了头号公敌，因为你基本上是在揭露保险行业的真面目。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Uh highly opaque, you know, what I would say overly complex profit-seeking entity.
zh: 呃，高度不透明，我想说，过度复杂的逐利实体。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're also going after the people that represent the companies that you want to move over.
zh: 不对——[[184]] 而你去做一个类似的产品，也许更好的产品，但用一种完全不同的、你知道的、更对齐的商业模式。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're saying, I'm calling people out.
zh: 而你是在说，我在点名批评这些人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I always want to be fair with this statement.
zh: 我对这句话一直想保持公正。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The smaller the employer group, usually the shadier the broker.
zh: 雇主团体越小，经纪人通常越不干净。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what I mean by this is they're going to be like, I'm going to get paid on everything and anything.
zh: 我这么说的意思是，他们会是这样：什么东西我都要拿钱，什么钱我都要赚。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The larger the client, you start to see, I would say, some professional behavior here and some more disclosures around compensation.
zh: 客户越大，你就会开始看到，我想说，一些职业化的行为，以及一些围绕薪酬的更多披露。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But the point of it is we had to fight against everyone, back to hand-to-hand combat, fix bayonets here.
zh: 但重点是，我们不得不对抗所有人，回到近身肉搏，上刺刀吧。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And because everybody in my mind was rotten.
zh: 因为在我心里，每个人都是烂的。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: This is kind of like classic, you know, counterpositioning, if you want to look at it that way.
zh: 这有点像经典的，你知道，反向定位，如果你愿意这么看的话。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Everybody's making money a certain way on a certain business model.
zh: 每个人都在用某种商业模式从某个生意里赚钱。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You're going to go and deliver a similar product, maybe a better product, but in a completely different business model that, you know, is more aligned.
zh: 你要去交付一个类似的产品，也许是一个更好的产品，但采用的是一种完全不同的商业模式，你知道的，一种更契合的商业模式。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: But because of the setup, you know, sometimes you get lucky where it's kind of like the big guys just ignore you, like, ah, yeah, let them let them do that.
zh: 但由于这种格局，你知道，有时候你会走运，就是那种大人物们干脆无视你，比如，啊，好吧，随他们去吧，让他们做那个去吧。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You know, the Netflix example being the obvious one.
zh: 你知道的，Netflix 的例子就是最明显的一个。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You know, let them run DVDs, whatever.
zh: 你知道的，随他们去做 DVD 租赁好了，管他呢。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: But in your case, probably not.
zh: 但在你的情况下，恐怕不是。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, how do you get started?
zh: 我是说，你是怎么起步的？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Where do you go?
zh: 你从哪里入手？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Because I'm thinking to convince the buyers is probably not easy, to convince the VCs is probably not easy.
zh: 因为我在想，说服买方可能不容易，说服 VC 可能也不容易。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, you have a track record, so maybe that helps.
zh: 我的意思是，你有履历，所以也许这有帮助。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: But, anyways, how do you get started on something like this?
zh: 但，总之，你是怎么在这样的事情上起步的？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah, you bootstrap.
zh: 是的，你靠自己白手起家(bootstrap)。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'm going to use the honest one.
zh: 我要用那个老实的说法。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I want to be fair.
zh: 而且我想保持公正。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Health technology was starting to become interesting, you know, 2016, 2017.
zh: 健康科技大约在 2016、2017 年开始变得有意思。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So there was a market there, but pharmacy benefits was observed to be this impossible fortress to get through because it was dominated by three massive players.
zh: 所以那里是有市场的，但药品福利被普遍认为是这座无法攻破的堡垒，因为它被三个巨头主导。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And no one had really had commercial success kind of overturning them.
zh: 而且之前没有人真正在推翻他们这件事上取得过商业上的成功。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what I mean by that is there have certainly been other pharmacy benefit managers, but they replicated the model.
zh: 我的意思是，当然也有过其他的药品福利管理公司，但它们复制的是同一个模式。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They did the same exact thing as the leaders in the market segment, and they grew to a certain point, and then they flatlined.
zh: 它们做的事和市场细分领域的领导者一模一样，然后增长到某个程度，就停滞了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: No one had ever scaled and started to take money from what I would call the two most valuable categories are Fortune 500 because they're large and prestigious.
zh: 没有人真正规模化，并开始从我会称之为最有价值的两个类别中赚取收入：一个是财富 500 强，因为它们规模大且有声望。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The second being health plans, because they're even bigger than Fortune 500 customers.
zh: 第二个是健康计划，因为它们比财富 500 强客户还要大。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So if you could service a health plan on the benefit and technology side, that's a huge deal.
zh: 所以如果你能在福利和技术层面服务一个健康计划，那是一件了不起的大事。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But no one had been able to do it.
zh: 但之前没有人能做到。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So, how do you get started?
zh: 那么，你们是怎么起步的？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We bootstrapped.
zh: 我们是自筹资金起步的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And when you bootstrap, you might have this vision of this powerful platform that's going to process claims and administrate patients and workflows.
zh: 当你自筹资金时，你脑海中可能会有这样一个愿景：一个强大的平台，能够处理理赔、管理患者和工作流。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But you're going to start with a small build and you're going to license third-party software.
zh: 但你必须从小规模的构建开始，并且你要去授权第三方的软件。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're not going to be thrilled with what you're given.
zh: 你不会对拿到的东西感到满意。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're going to have to rely upon third parties, you're going to have to license a network, you're going to have to work with other vendors, and you're not going to have a great product.
zh: 你将不得不依赖第三方，你将不得不授权一个网络，你将不得不和其他供应商合作，而且你不会有一个很棒的产品。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But you have to be willing to make some concessions, stay true to your principles, and understand if we do this correctly and we're able to scrap our way through these first couple of years, we'll start to build the platform we envision.
zh: 但你必须愿意做出一些妥协，同时坚守你的原则，并且明白：如果我们把这件事做对，能够艰难地熬过最初的一两年，我们就会开始构建我们设想的那个平台。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We'll have the opportunity to contract directly with pharmacies and other providers.
zh: 我们将有机会直接和药房以及其他服务提供方签约。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that's exactly what we did.
zh: 而这正是我们做的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But, you know, it's bootstrapping.
zh: 但是，你知道的，这就是自筹资金。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then in our second year, we did our Series A.
zh: 然后在第二年，我们做了 A 轮融资。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we finally felt with kind of the product market fit moment of that end of the second year where we had this inbound call from a prestigious customer.
zh: 所以到了第二年末，我们终于感觉到了某种产品市场契合的时刻——我们接到了一个有声望的客户的主动来电。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We felt like we had something that we could show.
zh: 我们觉得我们有可以拿得出手的东西了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The growth, the model was working, and that if someone would give us the money, we could scale it to be the organization we are today.
zh: 增长、模式都在运转，如果有人给我们钱，我们就能把它扩展成今天这样的组织。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Aaron Powell Did you raise like right out of the gate, like as soon as you had the idea?
zh: Aaron Powell 你们是一有想法就去融资了吗，就像一有想法马上就去？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So as soon as I had the idea, because in healthcare, you're going to have real costs because you have to register in states as a benefit manager or TPA.
zh: 我一有想法就去了，因为在医疗保健行业，你会有真实的成本，因为你必须以福利管理公司或 TPA 的身份在各个州注册。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're going to carry costs of personnel.
zh: 你还要承担人员成本。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, you're going to have service people, billing, finance people, et cetera.
zh: 你知道的，你要有服务人员、账务、财务人员，等等。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So you have real costs in your first year.
zh: 所以第一年你就有真实的成本。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we raised uh three and a half million dollars, I think was the exact number.
zh: 所以我们融了，呃，350 万美元，我记得准确的数字就是这个。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We closed in March of 2018.
zh: 我们在 2018 年 3 月完成交割。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I often say we were an operating company in healthcare, call it April.
zh: 所以我常说，大约在 4 月，我们就成了医疗保健行业的一家实际运营的公司。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And what was like V1 of the product?
zh: 那产品的 V1 版本是什么样的？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: One of the things I'm wondering is how much tech is there in this offering, in this product?
zh: 我想知道的是，这个服务、这个产品里到底有多少技术含量？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Back then, not a lot.
zh: 那时候，不多。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I want to be fair, there was technology, but it wasn't ours.
zh: 我想公平地说，是有技术，但那不是我们自己的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We were forced to license someone's claim processing platform.
zh: 我们被迫去授权别人的理赔处理平台。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We were forced to license someone's prior authorization workflow tool, someone's formulary management toolset.
zh: 我们被迫去授权别人的事先授权工作流工具、别人的处方集管理工具集。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We were outsourcing everything from reporting to printing solutions, you know, for cards.
zh: 我们把一切都外包了，从报告到卡片打印解决方案，你知道的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Um, so early days, the only thing that was proprietary from a technology side was how we were doing what we would call underwriting.
zh: 呃，所以在早期，技术方面唯一有专有性的，就是我们做所谓核保的方式。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we would bring in claims data, look at it, understand what we could do and how we could manage this account to a lower cost.
zh: 我们会引入理赔数据，去看它，理解我们能做什么、我们能如何把这个账户管理到更低的成本。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But over time, it would become an incredibly technology-focused company in the sense that at the core of our company is Judy, you know, and why are we called Judy?
zh: 但随着时间推移，它会变成一家极其以技术为核心的公司，因为我们公司的核心是 Judy，你知道的，我们为什么叫 Judy？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Judy short for adjudication, which is a fancy word for claim processing.
zh: Judy 是 adjudication（裁定）的简称，而 adjudication 是理赔处理的一个花哨说法。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so adjudication, in order to do it, just to visualize it, is hundreds of administrative workflows, like eligibility, who's in and out of a plan, plan design, like financial rule sets, what's her copay or coinsurance or out-of-pocket max.
zh: 那么裁定，为了能直观地想象它，就是数百个管理工作流，比如资格认定——谁在计划内、谁在计划外；计划设计——比如财务规则集——她的定额手续费、共同保险或自付上限是多少。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It's also clinical rule sets.
zh: 还有临床规则集。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Can I have this medication?
zh: 我能用这个药吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Did I meet the criteria therapeutically for this category, et cetera?
zh: 我在治疗上达到这个类别的标准了吗，等等？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, it's everything from billing to reimbursement to call center, client management, data and analytics, compliance, hundreds of work streams that in my competitors, many of them doing this stuff manually.
zh: 你知道的，从账务到报销到呼叫中心、客户管理、数据与分析、合规，有数百条工作流，而在我的竞争对手那里，其中很多东西他们都是靠人工完成的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So they'll have different systems and they stitch it together.
zh: 所以他们会用不同的系统，然后把它拼接在一起。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Our vision was could we effectively create what I call a supply chain version of healthcare, like an ERP, an enterprise platform for healthcare, where all of these work streams are operating in harmony next to each other, which will reduce costs.
zh: 我们的愿景是，我们能不能有效地创造一个我所说的医疗保健的供应链版本，就像一个 ERP，一个面向医疗保健的企业平台，让所有这些工作流彼此和谐地协同运转，从而降低成本。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So, you know, today, you know, we probably have about 1,600 employees, of which 500 is product and engineering.
zh: 所以，你知道的，今天我们大概有 1,600 名员工，其中 500 人是产品和工程。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And is Oscar Health, like are these kind of like health benefits platforms, are those comparables, are those competitors, or are they kind of approaching a different piece of the market, especially like at the beginning?
zh: 那 Oscar Health 呢，像这类健康福利平台，它们是同类可比对象、是竞争对手吗，还是它们切入的是市场另一块，尤其是在早期？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah, a different piece of the market, you know, is one to be fair, is we started with pharmacy benefits.
zh: 是的，是市场另一块，你知道的，公平地说，因为我们是从药品福利起步的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So in the United States, pharmacy and medical are actually administrated separately for what we call large companies.
zh: 所以在美国,对于我们所说的大型公司,药房和医疗实际上是分开管理的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So if you're self-insured in the United States, if you have a thousand covered lives, which is roughly you have 500 employees, you usually double it with the dependents and you have a thousand-person plan, you're self-insured.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Why do you want to be self-insured?
zh: 为什么你想自保?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Because your premium costs would be lower versus fully insured.
zh: 因为相比全额投保,你的保费成本会更低。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You could pay your own bills effectively.
zh: 你实际上可以自己支付账单。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what we did is we focused on the self-insured marketplace and we started with pharmacy.
zh: 我们所做的是专注于自保市场，我们从药房开始。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It was my background, plus, I felt as if we had, I think, a very unique business proposition back to the product market fit.
zh: 这是我的背景，另外，我觉得回到产品市场契合度这个话题，我们有一个我认为非常独特的商业主张。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so that's where we started.
zh: 所以我们就是从那里起步的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We would we would later expand into what I call TPA services, third-party administrator on the medical side.
zh: 我们后来会扩展到我所称的 TPA 服务，也就是医疗方面的第三方管理员。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So again, similar product on the administrative side to pharmacy, same concept, focus on self-insured.
zh: 所以再强调一下，在行政端是和药房类似的产品，同样的理念，专注于自保。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I go back to, you know, our competitors are CVS, Cigna United.
zh: 所以我回到，你知道的，我们的竞争对手是 CVS、Cigna、United。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Taking back to maybe like whether it's the first customer or one of the first customers, I'm really curious as to what the value proposition was like back then, how you framed it, and how you got them.
zh: 回到可能像是第一个客户或最早的客户之一这个问题，我真的很好奇当时的价值主张是什么样的，你们是怎么定位的，以及你们是怎么拿下他们的。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You know, to use your your product, unproven product, right?
zh: 你知道的，让他们用你们的产品，一个未经证实的产品，对吧？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: In something that you just said is so kind of uh not the sort of thing you tend to take risks with.
zh: 你刚才说的那件事，正是那种你不太会去冒险的事情。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Oh well, it is people ask me all the time, like, hey, would you ever want to go back to the good old days?
zh: 哦，总是有人问我，比如，嘿，你想回到过去的好日子吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're like, never.
zh: 然后你会说，绝不。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're like, why?
zh: 他们问，为什么？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I go, Do you know how hard it is to sell healthcare?
zh: 我就说，你知道卖医疗保健有多难吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And this is your pitch.
zh: 而这就是你的推销词。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Think about it.
zh: 想想看。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're like, customer asked me, how long have you been in business for?
zh: 他们说，客户问我，你们营业多久了？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, including this month.
zh: 我说，算上这个月。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they're like, Are you being funny?
zh: 他们问，你在开玩笑吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're like, no, I've been in business for three months now.
zh: 你说，不，我到现在已经营业三个月了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, great.
zh: 比如，太棒了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they're like, um, tell me about your other customers.
zh: 他们就像,嗯,跟我讲讲你的其他客户吧。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'm like, including you?
zh: 我说,包括你们吗?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they're like, you have no customers?
zh: 他们就说,你没有客户?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're like, no, not really.
zh: 你就说,对,基本没有。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And everything you have early adopters, and I'm sure you have them here, but there isn't as as compelling of a reason to be first on this as the like the risks kind of outweigh the cost, I think, for a lot of people's minds.
zh: 而且你所有的一切都是早期采用者,我相信你们这里也有,但在这个领域当第一名的理由不像……我觉得在很多人心里,风险有点盖过收益。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Because if you're first on, let's say, some AI-enabled outreach tool, it's like that's alpha.
zh: 因为如果你率先用上,比如说,某个 AI 驱动的外呼工具,那就像是一种 alpha。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You know, you're gonna reach more, like, yeah, let's try it, let's go.
zh: 你知道,你能触达更多,就像,对,试试吧,干起来。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Whereas with this, it's like worst case scenario is really bad, best case scenario, things work a little bit better, but yeah, I don't know.
zh: 而这个东西呢,最坏情况真的很糟,最好情况也就是事情稍微好一点,但,呃,说不准。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I don't know if I'm uh that's my assumption.
zh: 我不确定,呃,这只是我的猜测。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Well, that's what you're exactly right.
zh: 嗯,你说得完全正确。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Think about it, is most people are very conservative with benefits because they're like, I just want my people to have access to their care and have a reliable company.
zh: 你想想,大多数人对福利非常保守,因为他们觉得,我只是想让我的人能获得医疗服务,并且依托一家可靠的公司。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're trying to convince them that there's a problem that might be identified.
zh: 而你要去说服他们,说存在一个可能会被查出来的问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Some of my customers were like, my costs are going up and I can't figure out why.
zh: 我的一些客户会说,我的成本在涨,但我搞不清为什么。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So cost was the biggest driver, followed by service.
zh: 所以成本是最大的驱动因素,其次是服务。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They felt as if their members, as well as the plans experience, was substandard.
zh: 他们觉得自己的会员以及计划的体验都不达标。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, they felt like they were being discarded.
zh: 你知道,他们感觉自己被抛弃了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And to be fair, larger companies really don't like the small market.
zh: 而且说实话,大公司确实不喜欢小市场。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, they'd rather focus on big customers, Fortune 500.
zh: 你知道,他们更愿意专注于大客户,财富 500 强。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so when we started to talk to the small plans, we had to overcome this barrier, this wall of like, you have nothing to offer me because you have no experience.
zh: 所以当我们开始和小计划谈的时候,我们得跨越这道障碍、这堵墙,就是:你没什么能提供给我的,因为你没有经验。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: What we were able to do was to leverage the team's experience.
zh: 我们能做的,是利用团队的经验。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, hey, I've been in this industry for 18 years.
zh: 就像,嘿,我在这行干了 18 年。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'm gonna tell you all of my knowledge and I'm gonna tell you things you've never heard before.
zh: 我会把我所有的知识告诉你,我会告诉你一些你从没听过的事情。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I think it was that information, like, well, wait, wait, that makes sense.
zh: 我觉得正是这些信息让人觉得,等等,等等,这说得通。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, and that's true.
zh: 就是,而且这是真的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'm able to prove that in the data set.
zh: 我能在数据集里证明这一点。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so we were able to make observations in the data that I think was incredibly valuable to the customers, enough to overcome.
zh: 因此我们能够在数据中做出一些观察，我认为这对客户来说是极其宝贵的，足以克服。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're like, okay, you're telling me something I haven't heard.
zh: 他们会说，好吧，你告诉了我一些我从未听说过的东西。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're showing me where these costs are coming from, which no one has really been able to do with me.
zh: 你向我展示了这些成本是从哪里来的，这是之前没有人真正能够为我做到的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'll take a chance.
zh: 我愿意冒这个险。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I want to be fair.
zh: 而且我想公平地说。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I go back to my earlier statement.
zh: 我回到我之前的说法。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: These are 500, 1000 life cases that you're working with in your first year.
zh: 这些是你在第一年里经手的 500 到 1000 人的投保案例。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It's in that second year, it was almost immediately, once you had references, you could sell to a 4,000 life case.
zh: 到了第二年，几乎是立刻，一旦你有了参考案例，你就可以卖一个 4000 人的投保案例。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You could sell to an 8,000 life case.
zh: 你可以卖一个 8000 人的投保案例。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then I get the phone call of the large Fortune 500 company that says, hey, I've got 30,000 people here.
zh: 问题是，下一集要好得多，而你会错过它。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I've heard some really good things.
zh: 我听说了一些非常好的东西。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're saying things no one has had the courage to say, and I agree.
zh: 你在说一些没有人有勇气说的话，而且我同意。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And we'd like to move in this direction.
zh: 我们想朝这个方向发展。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Do you remember the first customer you signed?
zh: 你还记得你签下的第一个客户吗？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Those probably smaller customers and how that happened?
zh: 那些可能是较小的客户，以及那是怎么发生的？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, I often say unions are very good early adopters when it comes to cost savings and service, because one, they want to make sure their membership is treated on a level like family.
zh: 你知道，我经常说，在成本节约和服务方面，工会是非常好的早期采用者，因为第一，他们想确保他们的成员被当作家人一样对待。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The second part is municipalities and public sector and unions, they have fixed budgets.
zh: 第二部分是，市政机构、公共部门和工会，他们有固定的预算。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, I often say if you work with a Fortune 500 plan, you know, if their cost goes up 5%, they just pay it.
zh: 你知道，我经常说，如果你和一家财富 500 强的计划合作，你知道，如果他们的成本上升 5%，他们就直接付了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: A union has to consider sustainability, you know, very precisely.
zh: 而工会必须非常精确地考虑可持续性。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: How many union does how much is the union dues that we have, how much goes to benefits, working with actuaries, how long can we maintain the benefit at this rate?
zh: 有多少个工会，我们的工会会费是多少，有多少用于福利，与精算师合作，我们能在这样的费率下维持福利多久？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Do we have an ample amount of membership to survive?
zh: 我们是否有足够的成员数量来维持生存？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, corporate America doesn't necessarily have the same sensitivity to price that unions do for the reason I just described.
zh: 你知道，美国企业界不一定像工会那样对价格敏感，原因就是我刚才描述的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so unions became at the heart of our business the first couple of years.
zh: 所以在前几年，工会成为了我们业务的核心。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, those first two years, you know, I would say I bleed taft-heartly in the sense that I will forever be very thankful for unions.
zh: 你知道，在那头两年，你知道，可以说我身上流淌着 taft-heartly 的血，从某种意义上说，我将永远非常感谢工会。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I also also will point out I am the son of a public school teacher who is a union member as well.
zh: 我还想指出，我是一名公立学校教师的儿子，我的母亲也是工会成员。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so I understand the importance that benefits play in the public sector and for unions because it is a critical part of their compensation package.
zh: 所以我理解福利在公共部门和工会中的重要性，因为它是他们薪酬方案中至关重要的一部分。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Oftentimes, you know, unions in public sector have very good benefits.
zh: 通常情况下，你知道，公共部门的工会福利非常好。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I'm really worried because listen, like you've been listening for like what, 10, 20, 30 minutes now?
zh: 我真的很担心，因为听着，你已经听了大概多久了，10、20、30 分钟了？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Clearly, you like it.
zh: 显然，你喜欢这个节目。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And the thing is, the next episode is way better and you're gonna miss it.
zh: 问题是，下一集会好得多，而你会错过它。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You're gonna miss it because you're not following the show.
zh: 你会错过它，因为你没有关注这个节目。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So take your phone out and hit that follow button.
zh: 所以拿出你的手机，按下那个关注按钮。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Were you able to promise and quantify like how much the cost?
zh: 你是否能够承诺并量化成本能降低多少？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like, was that the key value prop, right?
zh: 比如，那是核心的价值主张，对吧？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's like, hey, you're paying this much.
zh: 就像，嘿，你现在付这么多。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: A lot of it is like effectively price gouging.
zh: 其中很多实际上等同于价格欺诈。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: We're gonna bring your cost to this.
zh: 我们会把你的成本降到这个水平。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like, was that the simple version?
zh: 比如，就是这么简单的一个版本吗？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You have to compete on price.
zh: 你必须在价格上竞争。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, I always want to be fair about this.
zh: 你知道，我总是想在这件事上保持公平。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so you have to be able to demonstrate that in both your offering.
zh: 所以你必须能够在你的方案中证明这一点。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So normally there's like a third-party consultant that is hired to kind of be the person who's overseeing the process.
zh: 通常会有一个第三方顾问被雇来，作为监督整个过程的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They'll provide the data in which we submit a bid.
zh: 他们会提供数据，我们据此提交投标。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And based upon the cost analysis, they'll say a combination of two things.
zh: 基于成本分析，他们会说两件事的结合。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: One, your offering, and two, your contract.
zh: 第一，你的方案，第二，你的合同。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So you have to make sure, obviously, if you're the consultant, that the contract matches the offering.
zh: 所以如果你是顾问，你显然必须确保合同与方案相匹配。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So someone can be like, hey, I repriced the claims and here's my offering.
zh: 因为有人可能会说，嘿，我重新为理赔定价了，这是我的方案。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But if the contract has a hundred different holes in it that you don't have to support that pricing once the plan is live, it's not worth the paper it was written on.
zh: 但如果合同里有一百个不同的漏洞，使得计划上线后你不必支持那个定价，那它就一文不值。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so it's that combination, but you're always competing on price.
zh: 所以是这两者的结合，但你总是在价格上竞争。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Aaron Powell And fundamentally, your your model at the beginning was you just charge, like you go back to square one.
zh: Aaron Powell 从根本上说，你们最初的模式就是直接收费，就像你回到起点一样。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like you're just gonna say this is the cost per participant, and you don't make money on each of the kind of the drugs, right?
zh: 就像你会说这是每位参与者的成本，而你不从那些药上面赚钱，对吧？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So this is the hard part as well, is my competitors are saying their services are free.
zh: 所以这也是难的地方，我的竞争对手说他们的服务是免费的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're gonna be like, wait, what?
zh: 你会说，等等，什么？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And be like, because their money they're taking is out of the drug spend, they don't charge a flat administrative fee.
zh: 然后会说，因为他们赚的钱是从药品支出里拿的，他们不收固定的管理费。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So in the column where it says admin fee in the analysis, you know, we'll have something that says, hey, we're gonna charge you $150,000 to manage this plan.
zh: 所以在分析里写着管理费的那一栏，你懂的，我们会有一个写着，嘿，我们要收你 15 万美元来管理这个计划。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And my competitors will have a zero.
zh: 而我的竞争对手那一栏会是零。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Let me tell you, it's hard to compete with a zero if people are just glossing through a presentation, but the net cost was working out in our favor.
zh: 我告诉你，如果人们只是粗略浏览演示文稿，很难和一个零竞争，但净成本算下来是对我们有利的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I try and point this out, which is we could never compete early on on what I call gross purchasing power.
zh: 而我试着指出这一点，那就是早期我们永远无法在我所谓的总购买力上竞争。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so if my competitors could get a drug, let's just say for $100, because we were smaller, maybe we paid $110 for that drug through our arrangement.
zh: 所以如果我的竞争对手能拿到一种药，假设 100 美元，因为我们规模更小，也许通过我们的安排我们要为那种药付 110 美元。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So people would be like, well, you would lose.
zh: 所以人们会说，嗯，你会输。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But there's two lines in any business there's obviously your gross revenue and there's your net.
zh: 但任何生意都有两条线，显然是你的总收入，还有你的净收入。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we had to beat them in operating efficiency.
zh: 所以我们必须在运营效率上击败他们。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So if you read my business plan at the start, it was we need to operate 70% more efficient than three Fortune 15 companies.
zh: 所以如果你一开始读我的商业计划书，里面写的是我们需要比三家财富 15 强公司运营效率高 70%。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Now, their purchasing power was higher, but if we operated that at that efficiency, we could beat them head to head.
zh: 现在，他们的购买力更高，但如果我们以那种效率运营，我们就能正面对抗击败他们。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And we could do something no one had ever done before, which is scale that model and start taking Fortune 500 business away from them.
zh: 而且我们能做到一件以前没人做过的事，那就是扩展这个模式，开始从他们手里抢走财富 500 强的生意。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that's exactly what we did.
zh: 而这正是我们做了的事。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: That lowers your net cost.
zh: 这降低了你的净成本。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: But then the other side of that, if I'm understanding it correctly, is you also charge everybody the same rate for the drug to begin with.
zh: 但另一面，如果我理解正确的话，是你一开始对每个人都收同样的药价。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So you're kind of fixing your margin.
zh: 所以你有点在固定你的利润率。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That's one of the beauties of the entire model.
zh: 那是整个模式的美妙之处之一。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And something that happened, I'm gonna say, a little bit by of luck and a little bit of pressure, is the Department of Labor and legislative bodies started to look into the cost of drug spend in this country.
zh: 而发生的一件事，我要说，有一点运气成分也有一点压力，是劳工部和立法机构开始调查这个国家的药品支出成本。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they started to have more scrutiny.
zh: 而他们开始有了更多审查。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They wanted more reporting, more oversight.
zh: 他们想要更多报告、更多监督。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And this was putting pressure on our competitors as well.
zh: 这也在给我们的竞争对手施加压力。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And we were obviously rising at that same time and appearing as the only reasonable solution to these, you know, what I would say conflicts of interest and other problems in the traditional PBM pharmacy benefit model.
zh: 而我们显然在同一时期崛起，并作为对这些问题唯一合理的解决方案出现，我会说是传统 PBM 药品福利模式中的利益冲突和其他问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so that for us was the beginning of everything, which was once we started to scale, once we had that product market fit moment, and then we had this tailwind of what I would say the press, legislative rules coming out, I would say disclosures being required by the Department of Labor that governs self-insurance in the United States.
zh: 所以对我们来说那是一切的开始，也就是一旦我们开始扩展，一旦我们有了那个产品市场契合的时刻，然后我们有了这股顺风，我会说是媒体报道、立法规则出台，我会说是劳工部要求披露，劳工部管理着美国的自保。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so for us, we were like right place, right time.
zh: 所以对我们来说，我们就是天时地利。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: When did those tailwinds like really start to take off?
zh: 那些顺风是什么时候真正开始起飞的？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that's kind of and you're like, that's that's later.
zh: 然后那有点，你会说，那是那之后了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So not to geek out on you, but in 2021, in the middle of what was the Consolidated Appropriations Act, which was, you know, like a stimulus bill on some level, was an amendment to ERISA, the Employee Retirement Investment Savings, you know, Act.
zh: 不想跟你说得太技术细节，但在 2021 年，在《综合拨款法案》中间，你知道，某种程度上像一项刺激法案，有一项对 ERISA 的修正案，也就是《雇员退休投资储蓄法案》，你懂的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And ERISA governs 401k and pension, but it also governs self-insurance.
zh: 而 ERISA 管理 401k 和养老金，但它也管理自保。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And it was amended by the Department of Labor at their request, and it made it into the CAA, the Consolidated Appropriations Act.
zh: 它由劳工部应他们的要求修订，并被写进了 CAA，《综合拨款法案》。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And it basically required full disclosure on all compensation for healthcare.
zh: 它基本上要求对医疗保健的所有报酬进行完全披露。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Now, it came out in December of 21.
zh: 现在，它是在 21 年 12 月出台的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: 22 was like a grace period.
zh: 22 年像个宽限期。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: 23 people needed to start reporting this information.
zh: 23 年人们需要开始报告这些信息。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: People being pharmacy benefit managers and administrators like ourselves had to start reporting this information.
zh: 人们，也就是药品福利经理和像我们这样的管理方，必须开始报告这些信息。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what we realized is people were faking it.
zh: 而我们发现人们在造假。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They either weren't doing it or they were providing example data.
zh: 他们要么根本没做，要么提供的是示例数据。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So instead of saying this is exactly how much money we made, and this was very easy for us because if you just charge a flat fee per claim, this is what we made.
zh: 所以不像说这就是我们确切赚了多少钱，这对我们来说非常容易，因为如果你按每次理赔收固定费用，这就是我们赚的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But my competitors had to suddenly contemplate am I going to disclose what I'm making on spread pricing, acquisition costs, 340B, rebates, performance management fees, you know, they like price protection, they have all these revenue streams.
zh: 但我的竞争对手突然不得不思考我是否要披露我在价差定价、采购成本、340B、返利、绩效管理费上赚了什么，你懂的，像价格保护，他们有所有这些收入流。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And to break it out by client would be almost impossible.
zh: 而且要按客户拆分几乎是不可能的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so that's when I think the consulting industry started to ask more questions.
zh: 所以我想那就是咨询行业开始提出更多问题的时候。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so 2024, I often say, was this year in which transparency mattered.
zh: 所以 2024 年，我常说，是透明度重要的那一年。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like suddenly people were like, at a large scale, our potential customers were all asking the same question.
zh: 就像突然之间人们，在大规模上，我们的潜在客户都在问同一个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Who's transparent?
zh: 谁是透明的？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Who's ethical?
zh: 谁是讲道德的？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Who's a good partner to work with?
zh: 谁是好的合作伙伴?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that just accelerated us even more.
zh: 而这让我们加速得更多。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So let's talk.
zh: 那么我们来聊聊。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, there's two kind of tactical areas we want to go deep on.
zh: 我是说,有两个比较战术性的领域我们想深入探讨。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: The first one is really around go to market.
zh: 第一个真的是围绕 go to market(进入市场)。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, the first two years you got yourself a 10 billion ARR before you really had any inbound, which means presumably all of it was outbound.
zh: 我是说,头两年你在基本没有任何 inbound(入站咨询)的情况下就做到了 100 亿 ARR,这意味着大概全都是 outbound(出站销售)。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And you talked a lot about selling through testimonials.
zh: 而且你讲了很多通过客户证言来销售的事。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And you mentioned even before the idea of bootstrapping, the fact that a lot of these won't sign up with you unless you have reference customers.
zh: 你甚至在提到 bootstrapping(自力更生)之前就说过,很多客户除非你有参考客户,否则不会跟你签约。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: How did you go to market for the first two years?
zh: 头两年你是怎么做 go to market 的?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: How did you get the first few million in revenue?
zh: 你是怎么拿到头几百万收入的?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: What worked?
zh: 什么方法有效?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Well, first of all, super lean.
zh: 嗯,首先,极度精简。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I was just telling a story this morning where we had to put a press release out, I think, for next week.
zh: 我今天早上刚讲了一个故事,我们不得不在下周之前发一份新闻稿,我记得是。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And normally that costs like $2,000.
zh: 通常那要花大概 2000 美元。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I used to lose my mind when someone would say we're going to do a press release for $2,000.
zh: 以前每当有人说我们要花 2000 美元发一份新闻稿,我都会抓狂。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'd be like, don't pay.
zh: 我会说,别付钱。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We'll do it.
zh: 我们自己来。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we did zero marketing the first two years.
zh: 所以头两年我们做的是零营销。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Zero.
zh: 零。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And we wouldn't sponsor anything.
zh: 我们不赞助任何东西。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We really wouldn't go to anything.
zh: 我们真的不去参加任何活动。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We wouldn't do anything.
zh: 我们什么都不做。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We wouldn't spend on search or any type of sponsorship programs for conferences.
zh: 我们不在搜索上花钱,也不为会议做任何类型的赞助项目。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We just wouldn't do it.
zh: 我们就是不干这些。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And my thought was let's spend the money to make sure we operate at the highest level of service.
zh: 我的想法是,让我们把钱花在确保我们以最高水平的服务水平运营上。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then our customers will become our brand managers.
zh: 然后我们的客户会变成我们的品牌管理者。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They will become our best brand ambassadors.
zh: 他们会变成我们最好的品牌大使。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They will be more than willing to tell other people what a great job we do.
zh: 他们会非常愿意告诉别人我们做得多好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that proved to be a very powerful hunch in healthcare.
zh: 而事实证明,在医疗健康领域,这是一个非常有力的直觉。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I always want to make that very clear.
zh: 我总是想把这一点说清楚。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: May not translate to other industries, but it certainly did for healthcare.
zh: 它可能不适用于其他行业,但在医疗健康领域确实如此。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: For the point that I stated earlier, there's no shortcuts, and people are very cautious when they buy healthcare.
zh: 基于我前面说过的那点,没有捷径可走,人们在购买医疗健康服务时非常谨慎。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so it was incredibly powerful to just be like anyone can call someone up on the phone and say, hey, I'm going to sell you something and do a great job.
zh: 所以,任何人都可以打个电话说,嘿,我要卖给你个东西,而且会做得很出色——这么说很容易。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But to actually have a customer that you know and respect say nice things about the company you're considering, that's game changing.
zh: 但如果你认识和尊敬的一位客户真的在夸你正在考虑的这家公司,那就完全是改变局面的。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Tactically.
zh: 具体战术上呢。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So you had what you didn't do, which you didn't spend on marketing, and you try to double down on this customers of brand ambassadors.
zh: 所以你有了你不做的事情,也就是不在营销上花钱,而且你试图加倍押注这种「客户即品牌大使」的思路。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: How do you do that tactically?
zh: 你在战术上是怎么做的?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Imagine I'm selling to health or I'm selling an enterprise.
zh: 想象我在卖医疗健康产品,或者我在向一家企业销售。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like I want to follow this playbook.
zh: 就是说,我想照搬这个打法。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: How do I do it?
zh: 我该怎么做?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I always go back to we had to look at what is a reflection of good service in our industry.
zh: 我总是回到这一点:我们必须审视,在我们的行业里,什么是优质服务的体现。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Good service starts with your membership.
zh: 优质服务始于你的会员。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Because if your membership is unhappy, the plan sponsor, the employer, becomes unhappy very quickly because HR is going to be overwhelmed with tales of woe and frustration.
zh: 因为如果你的会员不满意,计划发起方、雇主很快也会不满意,因为 HR 会被各种诉苦和抱怨淹没。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so the first thing we wanted to do is to make sure we had a world-class call center.
zh: 所以我们想做的第一件事,就是确保我们有一个世界级的呼叫中心。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And people are going to be like, that sounds so old school.
zh: 人们会说,这听起来太老派了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, yeah, it is on some level.
zh: 而我会说,是的,从某种层面上说确实是。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But what made us different is because we had no secrets.
zh: 但让我们与众不同的是,因为我们没有任何秘密。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So think about this.
zh: 想想看。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Imagine you're a customer service representative at a traditional insurance company, and someone goes, Well, why was it this price?
zh: 想象你是一家传统保险公司的客服代表,有人问,嗯,为什么是这个价格?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They can't answer that question because there's 600 different prices for that same drug.
zh: 他们无法回答这个问题，因为同一种药有600种不同的价格。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, uh, it's just what your price is, you know, and they you know, like, why?
zh: 你知道，呃，就是看你的价格是多少，你知道，他们，你知道，比如说，为什么？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Or like, or I paid X this month and next month it's Z, like what occurred?
zh: 或者说，我这个月付了X，下个月就变成Z了，这是发生了什么？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And it's very difficult for them to answer these questions.
zh: 而他们很难回答这些问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That was the first observation.
zh: 这是第一个观察。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So, what were we doing and investing in is to make sure that one, when someone called 99% of the time, someone who's calling for healthcare into a call center, they're not coming from a happy place.
zh: 所以，我们在做和投入的是确保第一，当有人打电话来的时候，99%的情况下，打医疗健康电话到呼叫中心的人，都不是从一个开心的状态打来的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so we must give them honesty.
zh: 所以我们必须给他们诚实。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We must be able to answer every question, even if it's not what they want to hear.
zh: 我们必须能够回答每一个问题，即使那不是他们想听的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But then we have to provide a solution.
zh: 但然后我们必须提供一个解决方案。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I want first call resolution at like 97% plus.
zh: 我想要首次呼叫解决率达到97%以上。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And why is that?
zh: 为什么要这样呢？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Because the worst thing in the world is you have a healthcare issue and you say, uh, like, see if that works and call back.
zh: 因为世界上最糟糕的事情就是，你有一个医疗健康问题，然后对方说，呃，比如，看看那个行不行，然后再打回来。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: No.
zh: 不行。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so that meant staying on the line eight, nine, 10 minutes.
zh: 所以那就意味着在电话上待八、九、十分钟。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I threw average handle time out the window.
zh: 所以我把平均处理时长扔出了窗外。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I didn't cap anyone, like, hey, you're judged on average handle time and you need to get off the phone in five minutes.
zh: 我不给任何人设上限，比如，嘿，你按平均处理时长被考核，你得在五分钟内挂电话。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I mean, it's like, I don't know if you remember the Zappos philosophy.
zh: 我的意思是，就像，我不知道你是否还记得Zappos的理念。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It's like, stay on the phone as long as you want with the customer.
zh: 就是，只要客户愿意，你想和客户在电话上待多久就待多久。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And this was like in-house call center that you had?
zh: 而这是你们自建的呼叫中心？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: In-house, yeah.
zh: 自建的，是的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Domestic.
zh: 国内的。

speaker: unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, you're like, whoa.
zh: 你知道，你会觉得，哇。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But what I knew was if we were bringing noise to like nothing, and this is what customers were saying.
zh: 但我知道的是，如果我们把噪音降到几乎没有，而这就是客户说的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're like, I'm not hearing any complaints.
zh: 他们说，我没听到任何投诉。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: In fact, people have actually gone out of their way to say this was a really good experience.
zh: 事实上，人们甚至特意来说这是一次非常好的体验。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That is gonna set the tone with the customer.
zh: 这会为定下客户的基调。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then what you're gonna do with the customer is you're gonna do something that is not going to be price efficient, which is we would go on site to actually go over the review with the customer.
zh: 然后你对客户要做的是，你会做一些在价格上不划算的事情，那就是我们会亲自上门和客户一起过一遍评审。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So at a minimum, you have quarterly reports and you have an annual review.
zh: 所以至少，你有季度报告和年度评审。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I was like, we're going to every single one of our customers.
zh: 而我说，我们要去拜访我们的每一个客户。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You've gone once a year or four times for each quarter?
zh: 你们是每年去一次，还是每个季度去一次共四次？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Well, you have four reviews.
zh: 嗯，你们有四次评审。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And my whole point was if someone wanted us to go on site, we would.
zh: 而我的重点是，如果有人想让我们上门，我们就会去。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But most people are like, coming here once a year.
zh: 但大多数人都是，一年过来一次。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That's enough.
zh: 这就够了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: That's enough.
zh: 够了。

en: Enough of you.
zh: 你们待够久了。

en: I don't want to see you here.
zh: 我不想在这里看到你们。

en: A lot of our customer concentration was mid-Atlantic Northeast when we started.
zh: 我们刚开始的时候，客户集中在大西洋中部和东北部地区。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I must have been in a rental car so much with my colleagues going out to Pennsylvania, to Maryland, to Delaware, Connecticut.
zh: 我肯定和同事们开着租来的车跑了很多趟，去宾夕法尼亚、马里兰、特拉华、康涅狄格。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: It didn't matter.
zh: 无所谓哪里。

en: I'm like, we have to get in front of them.
zh: 我说，我们必须出现在他们面前。

en: And as we expanded, you know, now I'm hopping on a flight.
zh: 随着我们扩张，你知道，现在我要跳上飞机。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, we're we're in Ohio.
zh: 你知道，我们在俄亥俄。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's funny.
zh: 很有意思。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: This is the thing about startups, is like, yeah, you know, having having done one, it's like on the outside, you know, there's so much glamour around it, so much hype.
zh: 这就是创业公司的事情，就像，是的，你知道，做过一次之后，就像，从外面看，你知道，围绕它有太多光鲜，太多炒作。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And then it's like, it's actually you driving in a rental car in some like little town, you know, nobody around.
zh: 然后实际上却是你开着租来的车在某個小城镇里，你知道，周围没人。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And it's like three hours just for you to have a meeting where they're like, cool, thank you so much.
zh: 而且花了三个小时就为了开一个会，然后他们就说，好，非常感谢。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like, and you're like, okay, that's my day.
zh: 比如，然后你就想，好吧，这就是我的一天。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And it's terrible.
zh: 而且这很糟糕。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, you know, like I will be fair, like the first couple of times you get really pumped and excited.
zh: 就是,你知道,公平地说,头几次你会非常兴奋、非常激动。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you're like, I have a customer and they want to talk to us, and this is so exciting.
zh: 你会觉得,我有一个客户,他们想和我们谈谈,这太让人激动了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But then by the time you're it's like your 78th, you know, kind of one of these, you're just like, I think we could make a the earlier flight if we hurry.
zh: 但等到你做到第 78 次这种事的时候,你就只会想,我觉得我们要是抓紧点,还能赶上早一点的航班。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,完全正确。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But no, it is not glamorous or sexy.
zh: 不过,这确实不光鲜,也不性感。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But when you are engaging with the customer, and I think this is important, this is I think really helpful advice is you know, we have hundreds of customers and we service millions of lives here directly.
zh: 但当你真正在与客户互动时——我认为这很重要,我觉得这是非常有用的建议——你知道,我们有数百个客户,我们直接服务着数百万人的生活。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm still the client manager on two of our oldest accounts.
zh: 而我仍然是两个最老账户的客户经理。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And people are like, why would you, as the CEO, be an account manager?
zh: 人们会说,为什么你作为 CEO,要去做客户经理?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I go, Because I have a direct line to the feedback, what's working, what's not, what keeps them up at night, what could we do better?
zh: 我会说,因为我有一条直达反馈的通道——什么在起作用,什么没有,什么让他们夜不能寐,我们还能做得更好什么?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I always want to say, like, yeah, is that in some sort of KPI report or, you know, someone giving me a presentation?
zh: 而我总是想说,比如,是的,这些难道不是在某种 KPI 报告里,或者某人给我做的演示文稿里吗?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I go, yes.
zh: 我会说,是的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But what keeps it what I would say honest and direct and raw is working with those customers.
zh: 但让这一切保持诚实、直接和原始的,正是与那些客户的直接合作。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I never gave up two of them, still to this day.
zh: 我从来没有放弃过其中两个,直到今天仍然如此。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So that's how you have this is like half the battle because you provide a great service, you're on top with your customers, your customers should be happy.
zh: 所以这就是你——这算是成功了一半,因为你提供了很棒的服务,你和客户关系紧密,你的客户应该会满意。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Are you actively turning that into testimonials, or are you just doing it reactively where it's you're selling and they're like, hey, anybody else?
zh: 那你是在主动把这些转化为推荐证言,还是只是被动应对——就是你在销售,然后他们说,嘿,还有其他人在用吗?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And you're like, Yeah, sure, call these guys.
zh: 然后你说,嗯,当然,打电话给这些人吧。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Or are you doing something a little bit more proactive to get them kind of as brand ambassadors talking about you on your behalf?
zh: 还是你在做一些更主动的事情,让他们成为品牌大使,代表你为你宣传?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Sure.
zh: 当然有。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So now we're a little bit more sophisticated.
zh: 所以现在我们做得更成熟一些了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we ask everyone to participate in our annual survey for customer support and service.
zh: 我们会请每个人参与我们针对客户支持与服务的年度调查。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so the typically head of HR or the head of total rewards or benefits at an organization is doing this review session and you know, filling in our rating.
zh: 通常是一家组织的 HR 负责人或整体薪酬福利负责人在做这个评审,并填写我们的评分。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But one of the questions we ask is, can we use you as a reference?
zh: 但我们问的问题之一是,我们可以把你作为参考推荐吗?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And that is extraordinarily important.
zh: 这一点极其重要。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then we have another line and says, Would you ever be interested in doing a conference with us?
zh: 然后我们还有另一行写道,你是否有兴趣和我们一起参加一个大会?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we have an annual conference for our customers or a panel or, you know, a featured broadcast of some sort.
zh: 所以我们有一个面向客户的年度大会,或者是小组讨论,或者某种形式的专题直播。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And, you know, you'll get people that are a little bit shy.
zh: 你知道,你会遇到有点害羞的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You'll get people that are like, I would like to do it, but my company is just, they're so difficult.
zh: 你也会遇到这样的人,说,我愿意参加,但我的公司——他们太难搞了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, we're a Fortune 500 company, it's very difficult for me to get approval to say anything about anything.
zh: 你知道,我们是财富 500 强公司,我要获得批准去谈论任何事都非常困难。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But you still get people that do.
zh: 但你仍然能找到愿意做这件事的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so you are being proactive to find the people that are allowed and willing to do it.
zh: 所以你要主动去找到那些被允许并且愿意做这件事的人。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So let's shift gears.
zh: 那么,让我们换个话题。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: The other thing that I thought you were doing very well was on the hiring side.
zh: 我觉得你做得很好的另一件事是招聘方面。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You you said you had about 90% retention for employees after four years, which is incredible because there's a lot of turnover in you know, in in tech and all these kind of startups.
zh: 你说过,四年之后你的员工留存率大约是 90%,这非常了不起,因为你知道,在科技圈和这类创业公司里,人员流动非常频繁。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Um, the key you said was really hiring for mission.
zh: 嗯,你说过关键是围绕使命来招聘。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So I'm curious on just your hiring approach, especially the first 30, 40, 50 employees, like how did you go about hiring them?
zh: 所以我很好奇你的招聘方式,尤其是最初 30、40、50 名员工,你是怎么招聘他们的?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: What did you do that was that was different, that was unique?
zh: 你做了什么不一样、什么独特的事情?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So the first 40 or so I was certainly involved with.
zh: 所以最初的 40 人左右,我肯定是亲自参与的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And if it wasn't me hiring or recruiting that person directly, it was certainly me being involved with a panel of review.
zh: 即便不是我亲自招聘或招募那个人,我也肯定会参与评审小组。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, hey, tell me why.
zh: 比如,嘿,告诉我为什么。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: These hires meant a lot.
zh: 这些招聘意义重大。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we do a meet the new hires meeting uh every Monday here in our company.
zh: 所以我们在公司里每周一都会开一个新员工见面会。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I tell this story when I meet the new hires, because I normally see a new class every Monday of 20 or 30 new people.
zh: 而我在见新员工时会讲这个故事,因为我通常每周一都会见到一批 20 到 30 人的新员工。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I mean, it's crazy.
zh: 我是说,这很疯狂。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And when they come in, you know, I tell them the story.
zh: 当他们进来的时候,你知道,我会给他们讲这个故事。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Once upon a time, we used to actually take you to dinner.
zh: 很久以前,我们实际上是会带你去吃晚饭的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We used to be like, hey, like it was such a huge moment that we hired someone this month.
zh: 我们以前会觉得,嘿,这个月招到一个人是多么重大的时刻。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We'd be like, all right, like Linda, we're taking you to dinner.
zh: 我们会说,好了,比如 Linda,我们要带你去吃晚饭。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they'd be like, all right.
zh: 他们会说,好啊。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But then over time that didn't scale.
zh: 但随着时间推移,这种做法没法规模化了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And then we used to call everybody.
zh: 然后我们过去会给每个人打电话。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like I used to call every you know, person individually, and be like, hey, welcome to the company.
zh: 比如我过去会单独给每一个人打电话,然后说,嘿,欢迎来到公司。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I want to introduce myself.
zh: 我想介绍一下我自己。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That didn't scale well with calendars.
zh: 那种方式在日历安排上扩展性不好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So now we do it as a group and it's a meet and greet.
zh: 所以现在我们以小组形式来做,就是一个见面会。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They introduce themselves, they ask a question of me, and it could be anything personal, business, experience, et cetera.
zh: 他们做自我介绍,向我提一个问题,可以是任何东西,个人的、业务的、经历等等。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And you know, it's the whole goal is for me to get to know them a little bit better and for them to get to know me a better.
zh: 你知道,整个目标就是让我更好地了解他们,也让他们更好地了解我。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Better.
zh: 更了解我。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But going back to your question is the piece that we kept finding over and over of people that were just our high performers, like our A players were the people that believed in the mission.
zh: 但回到你的问题,我们反复不断发现的一点是,那些属于我们高绩效者的人,像我们的 A 级选手,是那些相信使命的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like wholeheartedly.
zh: 比如,我想改变医疗保健。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, I want to change healthcare.
zh: 比如,我想改变医疗保健。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I want to improve healthcare.
zh: 我想改善医疗保健。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I think this is the way to do it.
zh: 而我认为这就是实现它的方式。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That made all the difference in the world.
zh: 这带来了天翻地覆的差别。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I do want to say something is people ask me, like, well, what do you mean by high performer?
zh: 我确实想说一点,有人问我,比如,你说的“高绩效者”是什么意思?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: High performer in my world is I say this all the time.
zh: 在我的世界里,高绩效者是——我一直这么说。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: D players see a problem and say nothing.
zh: D 级选手看到问题却什么也不说。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Hopefully, most companies don't have any of those people.
zh: 希望大多数公司都没有这种人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: C players see something and be like, hey, there's a problem.
zh: C 级选手看到一些东西,然后说,嘿,这里有个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And they report it to a supervisor or manager.
zh: 然后把它报告给主管或经理。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, the B players are like, hey, I saw, you know, this problem.
zh: 你知道,B 级选手会说,嘿,我看到了这个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You could do A or B to solve for this.
zh: 你可以做 A 方案或 B 方案来解决这个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Oh, okay.
zh: 哦,好的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You're giving me some solutions.
zh: 你在给我一些解决方案。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The A players see something and fix it.
zh: 而 A 级选手看到问题就直接把它修好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I never knew it even was a problem.
zh: 甚至我根本不知道那曾经是个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm stealing that from President Barack Obama, to be fair.
zh: 公平地说,这话是我从贝拉克·奥巴马总统那里借来的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I think that he has said that before.
zh: 我觉得他以前说过这个。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: A players for him do that.
zh: 对他来说,A 级选手就是那样做的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I couldn't agree more because when you're dealing with complex workflows and a human interaction, it's healthcare.
zh: 我非常赞同,因为当你要处理复杂的工作流程和人与人互动时,这可是医疗保健。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You want people, obviously, that care about the mission, but they're willing to solve, like to go beyond.
zh: 你显然想要那些关心使命的人,但他们也愿意去解决,愿意超越本职。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, hey, something is always going to break or fail on the system, but I'm going to fix it.
zh: 比如,嘿,系统总会有东西出故障,但我会去把它修好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I think those people, what they all have in common, believe in the mission.
zh: 而我认为那些人,他们的共同点就是,相信使命。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: So, I mean, there's kind of two parts to that.
zh: 所以,嗯,这大概有两个部分。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I'm curious how you tested for either the A-player side, people who are going to go and just fix things, and then the mission piece.
zh: 我很好奇你是怎么测试这两方面的,要么是 A 级选手那一面,就是那些会直接去把事情修好的人,然后是使命那一部分。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like, the problem with interviews is they're fakeable, they're gameable, you know, and especially something like mission.
zh: 比如,面试的问题在于它们是可以造假、可以被应付的,你知道,尤其是像使命这种东西。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Hey, you know, why do you want to work here?
zh: 嘿,你知道,你为什么想在这里工作?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Oh my God, it just health is so boring, what you guys are doing.
zh: 哦天哪,医疗太枯燥了,你们在做的事情。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's, you know, I'm going to transform an industry.
zh: 就是,你知道,我要改变一个行业。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, it'd be relatively easy for somebody to fake it, at least in terms of the words they say.
zh: 我是说,对某人来说造假其实相当容易,至少在他们说的话这个层面上。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: How did you learn to test for that in a way that was at least relatively accurate to reality?
zh: 你是怎么学会用一种至少相对贴近现实的方式来测试这一点的?

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So in the early days, I will be fair, is we wouldn't bring up the question or ask about it.
zh: 所以在早期,公平地说,我们不会主动提起这个问题,也不会去问它。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, why did you know?
zh: 比如,你为什么——你知道?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So we're trying to set someone up that is going to mention that they believe in the mission.
zh: 所以我们是在试图铺好场子,让对方自然提到他们相信使命。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: The second thing that we almost always listen for is someone who relates to a bad experience in healthcare.
zh: 第二件我们几乎总会留意倾听的事情,是有没有人提到自己在医疗保健方面的糟糕经历。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: That could be personal, that could be a family member.
zh: 那可以是亲身经历,也可以是家人相关的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I felt if those two things occurred, we had a high probability of this person's but you wanted it to come out naturally.
zh: 而我觉得如果这两件事都出现了,那这个人有很大概率——但你希望它是自然流露出来的。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: You're talking normal conversation.
zh: 你在正常地聊天。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: At some point, they say something like that.
zh: 在某个时刻,他们说了类似那样的话。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Can't ask.
zh: 没法直接问。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Just avoid it.
zh: 只能避开。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They have to bring it up.
zh: 必须由他们自己提出来。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And if they bring it up and the other end to this logic string is, and they shared something personal.
zh: 如果他们主动提出来了，这条逻辑链的尽头就是：他们分享了一些亲身经历。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like I have witnessed how bad healthcare is.
zh: 比如我亲眼见证了医疗保健有多糟糕。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Let me tell you why.
zh: 让我告诉你为什么。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Odds are this is personal.
zh: 那么大概率这是切身的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They want to fix it.
zh: 他们想解决这个问题。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They don't want anyone to experience what they or their family or their loved one or dependent went through.
zh: 他们不希望任何人再经历他们自己、或他们的家人、或他们所爱的人、或他们照护的人经历过的事。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Then we have a winner, most likely.
zh: 那么我们大概率就找到了一个赢家。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Not always, but very, very high probability.
zh: 不一定每次都对，但概率非常非常高。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And almost every single person, you know, that I go back to that are still with us, you know, from our first year, these are the people that absolutely demonstrated these characteristics.
zh: 而且几乎每一个第一年加入、至今还留在我们身边的熟人，都是绝对展现出了这些特质的人。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: What about the other half of that equation?
zh: 那这个等式的另一半呢？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: In other words, somebody who cares, who had a personal experience, they believe in the mission, but isn't an A player.
zh: 换句话说，一个人有热忱、有亲身经历、相信这个使命，但不是 A 级人才。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Like, how do you tell those two apart?
zh: 比如，你怎么区分这两者？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Somebody who's going to find problems and just fix them for you.
zh: 一种是会主动发现问题并直接帮你解决掉的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I want to say some of the a player characteristic year is going to be trial by fire.
zh: 所以我想说，A 级人才的部分特质是要经过烈火考验的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I want to be fair.
zh: 我想公平一点。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You put someone in a firefight, and then someone just goes into the bunker and curls up into a fetal position.
zh: 你把一个人放进战火里，有的人就直接躲进掩体，蜷缩成胎儿姿势。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so people are like, I'm with you.
zh: 而有的人会说，我跟你站在一起。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, how can I help you?
zh: 比如，我能怎么帮你？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, you know, there's the enemy.
zh: 比如，敌人在那边。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: How do we win?
zh: 我们怎么赢？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so I will be fair.
zh: 所以我要公平地说。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I do not have a test for who is an A player in the interview process, but I will say there's a strong correlation going back to people that believe in, you know, I often say, like, if you're a brilliant person, you can you can do anything.
zh: 我没有一套在面试流程中判断谁是 A 级人才的测试，但我要说，回到那些相信的人身上，存在很强的相关性。我常说，如果你是个才华横溢的人，你什么都能做成。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Honestly, you've got the world is yours for the taking.
zh: 说实话，整个世界都任你攫取。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So if you have someone who's super talented, but they're talking about this personal experience and an appreciation for your mission and business model, we're gonna go places.
zh: 所以如果你有一个极具天赋的人，同时他又在讲述这段亲身经历、并且认同你的使命和商业模式，那我们会走得非常远。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, and I just go back to that there's that high correlation between adoption and being a zealot on the mission and just being an A player because every day they're going in the back of their mind, how do I prevent people from experiencing this, this, this horrible healthcare experience?
zh: 你知道，我只是回到那个高相关性上：投入度、对使命的狂热、和成为 A 级人才之间的相关性很高，因为他们每天脑海里都在想，我怎么才能让别人不再经历这种可怕糟糕的医疗体验。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I mean, one of the things is when somebody believes in the mission or at least in the impact of what they're doing, they don't stop thinking about it.
zh: 我是说，其中一个关键点就是，当一个人相信这个使命，或者至少相信他们所做之事的影响力时，他们不会停止思考。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: I always I always thought about how do you, especially now that remote is is you know such a big thing, and even like the sort of work that people do is not mechanical.
zh: 我一直在想你怎么……尤其是现在远程办公已经成了这么大的趋势，而且人们做的工作也不是机械性的。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And yet it's it's e it's too, I don't really believe that hours don't matter, but I don't believe hours matter.
zh: 然而它……它也……我不真的相信工时不重要，但我也不相信工时重要。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And my reconciliation of it all was it's just mind share.
zh: 我对这一切的调和答案就是：心智占用。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's not so much like how when do you sit in front of the computer, when do you get up?
zh: 不在于你什么时候坐在电脑前、什么时候起身？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: It's when you go home, when you're watching TV, when you're doing other things, at some point, obviously you're not thinking.
zh: 而是当你回家、看电视、做别的事情的时候，当然，某些时刻你显然没在想。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: But how often are you just like you're like, oh, that thing?
zh: 但你有多频繁会突然想到，哦，那个事？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And then you come back the next day and you've you actually improve from the day before, the weekend before, right?
zh: 然后第二天回来，你真的比前一天、比上个周末有了进步，对吧？

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Because you're on it.
zh: 因为你一直惦记着它。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: And I mean, that just makes all the difference.
zh: 我是说，这就是天壤之别。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: No, I I couldn't agree more.
zh: 不，我完全同意。

en: I I think people that believe in emission and it's personally impacted them some part about it is to your point, it's ever present.
zh: 我……我认为那些相信使命、并且亲身被其影响的人，正如你所说，其中某个部分就是，它是无时不在的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: They're thinking about how can I fix it?
zh: 他们一直在想，我怎么能解决它？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: How can I do better?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I see it.
zh: 而且我看得见。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I I see it, you know, not just in you know what I'll call the breakfix category, but proactive on new product development, new feature sets.
zh: 我……我看得见，不只是在所谓的修复故障类问题里，还包括在新产品开发、新功能集上的主动作为。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, again, going back to how do I make a patient's life better?
zh: 你知道，又回到那个问题上，我怎么让病人的生活变得更好？

en: What about uh in terms of finding these candidates?
zh: 那么在寻找这些候选人方面呢？

zh: 你有没有……比如最早的 30、40 个员工，在主动寻访这方面你有没有做过什么有意思的事情？

en: Yeah.

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So all right.
zh: 好，好的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: First 40 employees I go to one degree of separation.
zh: 前 40 名员工，我只找一度人脉以内的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, is it someone I worked with or someone very close to me that I respect worked with this person?
zh: 你知道，就是和我共事过的人，或者我非常尊敬的、和我很亲近的人跟这个人共事过。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So I'll give you a great example.
zh: 那我给你举一个很好的例子。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Uh I was looking for someone on the implementation side.
zh: 呃，我当时在找一个落地实施方面的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: So this is someone who knows how to set up a benefit plan, which is extraordinarily difficult.
zh: 就是那种知道怎么搭建福利计划的人，这事儿极其困难。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I asked all around, because you know, I've been in healthcare for a while.
zh: 我到处打听，因为你知道，我在医疗行业干了一阵子了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I know people in different companies.
zh: 我认识不同公司里的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I'm like, who's the best person in implementation you've ever worked with?
zh: 我就问，你共事过的最厉害的实施人员是谁？

en: And I kept getting the same name.
zh: 然后我一直听到同一个名字。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: This woman by the name of Karen Durker, who still works with me here.
zh: 一个叫 Karen Durker 的女性，她现在还在我这里工作。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, what the heck is a Karen Durker?
zh: 我当时想，Karen Durker 到底是什么人？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, what are the odds?
zh: 我就想，这概率有多大？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Three different people both said the same name.
zh: 三个不同的人都说了同一个名字。

speaker: Pablo Srugo
en: Crazy.
zh: 太疯狂了。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what's interesting is she was not very senior in her company.
zh: 有意思的是，她在她公司里职位并不是很高。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, so this person gets their hands dirty, knows every aspect of implementation.
zh: 我就想，所以这个人愿意亲自动手，懂实施的每一个环节。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I have three people I respect very highly giving me.
zh: 而且有三个我非常尊敬的人向我推荐她。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And what's a really interesting story if as she tells it, she wasn't gonna go with us.
zh: 有个很有意思的故事，据她自己讲，她本来是不打算来我们这儿的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: She was just like, they're like small.
zh: 她就是觉得，他们规模很小。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, I don't like I don't know if they're gonna be in business next year.
zh: 就是，我不确定他们明年还能不能继续经营下去。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And she tells a story that she was going to bed and she turned to her husband, and her husband's like, I think you should do it.
zh: 她讲了一个故事，说她准备睡觉的时候，她转向她丈夫，她丈夫说，我觉得你应该去。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, I think this is going to be a great, you know.
zh: 就是，我觉得这会是一件很了不起的事，你知道。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Now she's the executive vice president in charge of all implementation at her company and probably commands a team of like, you know, 100 people here.
zh: 现在她是负责全公司所有实施工作的执行副总裁，可能领导着一支大概 100 人的团队。 [[663→续]] 但是我的重点是，她的推荐级别如此之高。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: But but my point is she came so highly recommended.
zh: 但是但是我的意思是她来的时候可是被高度推荐的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I I had to go with that.
zh: 我必须听从那个推荐。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And for my first 40, I really try and lean into did I work with them or somebody I respect, you know, and and that's an important qualifier because you know, I have a lot of friends and they may be like, oh, like Sal's great.
zh: 对我的前 40 名员工，我真的努力倾向于用「我和他们共事过，或者是我尊敬的人和他们共事过」这个标准，这是个重要的限定条件，因为你知道，我有很多朋友，他们可能会说，哦，Sal 特别棒。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'll be like, is Sal great or is Sal great to drink with it?
zh: 然后我会问，Sal 是特别棒，还是 Sal 是喝酒特别棒的伴儿？

en: You know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

en: Like we want to have a few margs, like Sal's our guy.
zh: 就是说，我们要喝几杯玛格丽塔，那 Sal 就是我们的人。

en: But if we want to implement a plan, Karen's our person.
zh: 但如果我们要落地实施一个计划，Karen 就是我们的人。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, but I I think that's where I felt we created a stable foundation getting back to the execution and operation, which was going to be critical because if you're starting and we didn't have those testimonials, I don't think we would be talking right now.
zh: 你知道，我觉得那就是我觉得我们打下稳定基础的地方，回到执行和运营上来，这会是至关重要的，因为如果你在创业，而如果我们没有那些客户见证，我不认为我们现在还能坐在这里谈话。

en: What would be a top piece of advice for you for like an early stage founder that's still looking for product market fit?

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: In the early days, all right.
zh: 在早期阶段，好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: This this is an opinion.
zh: 这只是一个观点。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: If you've never done your own business, I think a lot of people that I speak with get caught in this trap of they get super excited about the things that kind of glamorize your business.
zh: 如果你从来没有自己创过业，我采访过的很多人都会掉进这个陷阱：他们对那些能让你的生意显得光鲜亮丽的东西超级兴奋。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Like, hey, like the the website design and the what Pantone blue I used for the logo, and you know, you know, what is the shape of these things?
zh: 比如，嘿，比如网站设计啦、logo 用哪种 Pantone 蓝啦，你知道，这些东西的形状是什么？

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: What's the marketing around it?
zh: 它周围要做什么营销？ [[687→续]] 你知道，我们应该设披萨星期五，我们应该，你得把这些东西全部剔除掉。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You know, we should have Pizza Fridays, we should, you need to strip all of that out.
zh: 你知道，我们应该设立披萨周五，我们应该……你需要把这些全部剔除掉。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And this sounds like like pretty basic advice.
zh: 这听起来像是相当基础的忠告。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And I'm like, you have to treat your startup like this is the only money you're ever gonna see in your life, and that every single expense, including your time, because and I say this time is our most valuable asset.
zh: 而我会说，你必须把你的初创公司当作这是你这辈子唯一能看到的一笔钱来对待，每一笔开支，包括你的时间，因为我常这么说，时间是我们最宝贵的资产。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I can't buy it, I can't store it, can't replace it.
zh: 我买不到它，我存不住它，也换不回来。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: I didn't say this, Peter Drucker did, but I appreciate what that gentleman observed, and I've lived by it my entire life.
zh: 这话不是我说的，是 Peter Drucker 说的，但我很欣赏那位先生观察到的这一点，我一辈子都以此为准则。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And this is what I try and say do not waste your time on things that are cool.
zh: 这就是我想说的：不要把时间浪费在酷的东西上。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: Don't waste your time on things that you think are fun.
zh: 不要把时间浪费在你觉得好玩的东西上。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: You need people that go back to believe the mission, and what's fun for them is, in my case, making healthcare better.
zh: 你需要那些回到「相信使命」上来的人，对他们来说好玩的事，在我的情况下，就是让医疗变得更好。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And so that's what I want to spend.
zh: 所以那就是我想要投入的。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: All of our time, effort, and budget.
zh: 我们全部的时间、精力和预算。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: There's no safety net.
zh: 没有安全网。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: There's no series B, there's no series C.
zh: 没有 B 轮，没有 C 轮。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: We need to spend this money as if it's the only oxygen left in the room.
zh: 我们必须把这些钱花得就像它是房间里仅剩的氧气一样。

speaker: AJ Loiacono
en: And it it that level of financial discipline and time discipline, I don't think people appreciate enough.
zh: 而这种程度的财务纪律和时间纪律，我觉得人们没有给予足够的重视。
